title: useArrival claims every flight inside a database, so the dossier's own moves hold for 1.06 s
body:
## Summary
useArrival (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/useArrival.ts:139-159) re-runs its claim-and-dress chain on every flight while a database is staged, so opening or closing the dossier holds the kit's level flight "moving" for FLIGHT + DRESS (1,060 ms) and re-dresses the L1 labels behind the card.

## Description
The effect's dependencies are [claim, flightNo, reduced, staged.database]. A database is staged once, when the nav's group changes; but flightNo changes on EVERY nav move (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/state.ts:78-103 increments flight for openItem, up and abort too). So the L1 -> L2 move (open_item, a click on a card) and the L2 -> L1 move (closing the card) each re-run the effect: it claims the new flight (useLevelFlight then cannot self-settle it in a frame, examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useLevelFlight.ts:178-183), waits FLIGHT (620 ms), writes at: "dress" again, waits DRESS (440 ms), then releases. The file's own comment (useArrival.ts:107-111) says it "deliberately does NOT restage when the dossier opens over a database already arrived at" - the staging is skipped but the timers and the claim are not. While the claim is held, moving is true, and the nav's Escape means abort (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/nav.ts:112, escape.ts:79-84): close the card, press Escape again within a second, and abort returns to prev - the dossier - which is the hirelane bug flight.ts:83-85 describes ("a second Escape aborting back INTO the dossier"). Fixed: claim and dress only the flight that changed the group (capture the flight number when the group is staged, in a ref or in Staged), so a flight inside one database is left to self-settle.

## Flow
- the reader opens billing (L1); the arrival runs once, as designed
- the reader opens a table card (L2): flight n+1, the effect claims it, moving stays true 1,060 ms, the L1 labels re-run their dress beat under the card at +620 ms
- the reader closes the card (overlay Escape) and presses Escape again within 1 s to leave the database
- the nav reads moving = true and aborts instead of going up: focus returns to prev, the card reopens

## Expected impact
A reader leaving a database right after closing a card goes up instead of being thrown back into the card, and the card's open is not followed by a second, invisible dress. Measured by a hook driver: claims held and dress beats written per nav move inside one database (expected 0 after). Could break: the arrival's first-flight hold, if the captured flight is the wrong one - arrival.test.ts and a driver case for the first open must both stay green.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Escape after closing a card leaves the database instead of reopening the card
Before: walked from the code - 1 claim of 1,060 ms and 1 re-dress per open or close of a card inside a database; second Escape inside the window dispatches abort (escapeAbortsFlight true at level 1)
After: 0 claims and 0 re-dress on moves that keep the group; Escape after close dispatches up
Method: simulation - the effect is a React hook with timers and the kit's flight; no driver exists in this repo for useArrival (arrival.test.ts pins only the pure beatOf/inkable), and the abort case needs the window to confirm
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a hook driver for useArrival with React stood in (as test/spatial-model-tools.test.ts does for useRun) and a fake LevelFlight counting claim/release, plus the kit's nav reducer: open billing, open a table, up, Escape - count claims and dress writes per move, and the action the second Escape dispatches

title: No test runs the shell's 15 tool handlers, the three GATED ones included
body:
## Summary
examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx registers 15 tools - every write this page offers an agent, and the three GATED ones - and no test calls any of their handlers; tools.test.ts reads the registrations as source text and calls the library "minus the toast".

## Description
tools.test.ts:58-70 regex-reads name / reversible / sideEffects out of the file and checks the declared class; tools.test.ts:148-170 call lib/mutations directly. Nothing would notice read_pairs calling mergeAction, normalize_fields registered with sideEffects "none", or a write handler that never toasts or refreshes - the class a host's gate reads is published by the handler's registration (README 3.3, design 5.1), and the handler is the one thing never run. This round built the instrument for the Blocks' seven read tools (test/spatial-model-tools.test.ts: BlocksTools.tsx loaded as shipped, kit verbs real, driven through runTool on a scratch seed, negative control built in) and ledgerbox did the same for its 19 (examples/ledgerbox/test/tool-handlers.test.ts, 90f063f). HostCapabilities is in tidycrm-blocks-ui's paths, so it is carded. Fixed looks like: the same harness, with app/actions wrapped (names read off the module), next/navigation and the toast stood in, every one of the 15 driven, reads reaching no action and writing no revision or activity row, writes reaching exactly one action whose activity row is as reversible as declared.

## Flow
- extend the harness: stand-ins for @/app/actions (record, then run for real against the tempHome seed), next/navigation, @athena/demo-kit/ui
- HostCapabilities.tsx holds a JSX fragment (line 77), so either load its two inner components (SharedCapabilities, ShippedCapabilities) or give the loader a JSX transform
- one plausible call per tool; seed a read that writes and a write under another tool's class, watch both go red

## Expected impact
The class an agent's gate trusts for the page's writes is checked against what the handlers do. Could break nothing: test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the 15 shell handlers are driven against their declared class
Before: 0 of 15 handlers run by any test (grep: no test imports HostCapabilities; tools.test.ts reads it with readFileSync)
After: 15 of 15 driven, with a seeded control
Method: probe - counted the population and the readers; the harness for the other half was built this round (ed38e1c); not built here because the file is another context's
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/test/tools.test.ts:58-70  specs(file): read(file).split("useWebMCPTool({") - source text, not a render
examples/tidycrm/test/tools.test.ts:152  "resolve_pair's handler, minus the toast" - lib/mutations called directly
git grep -c "useWebMCPTool({" examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx -> 15
examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx:77  <SharedCapabilities counts={counts} />  (JSX: the .tsx strip loader cannot load it as is)
context-map.json: HostCapabilities.tsx is in tidycrm-blocks-ui
built this round for the other tool file: ed38e1c test/spatial-model-tools.test.ts (7 of 7 Blocks handlers)
instrument: examples/tidycrm/test/spatial-model-tools.test.ts's stand-in hooks extended to HostCapabilities' two inner components with app/actions wrapped and run on the tempHome seed; a seeded read-that-writes must go red

title: search_records and search_blocks cannot page past 25, and journey act 3 sends a limit the door refuses
body:
## Summary
search_records answers "showing 25 of 276" and search_blocks "showing 25 of 46" with no argument that reaches the rest, and examples/journey/tests/journey.spec.ts:516 asks search_records for { text: "", limit: 500 }, which the execute door refuses outright.

## Description
Both searches bound their answer with bounded(found, SEARCH_PAGE) (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/tools/search.ts:77, :118) and declare no page parameter (BlocksTools.tsx search_blocks / search_records parameters), so the cut is announced but cannot be walked: rows 26-276 of the sample are unreachable from search_records by any argument, and tables 26-46 from an unfiltered search_blocks. The journey's act 3 wants every contact id for a normalisation preview and sends limit: 500; the door validates against the closed published schema and answers {"ok":false,"error":"unknown argument \"limit\"; allowed: text, database"} (examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts:56-58), so itemsOf(...) is empty and the act's "contact ids to normalise" expectation fails. take.spec.ts:777 sends { text: "" } and silently gets 25 of 276. Fixed: an optional page argument on both searches through the kit's boundedPage (the envelope already carries page), and the journey paging instead of sending limit.

## Flow
- journey act 3: crm.read("search_records", { text: "", limit: 500 })
- door: unknown argument "limit" -> { ok: false }
- itemsOf -> [] -> expect(ids.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) fails
- with page: the journey walks pages 0..11 of 276 and previews them all

## Expected impact
An agent (and the journey) can read every sample row and every table a search announced. Could break: any caller that relies on page-less answers - none in tree besides the journey, which needs the edit.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every result a search announces can be reached by some argument
Before: probe on the scratch seed - search_records "" showing 25 of 276; search_blocks {} showing 25 of 46; runTool(search_records schema, { text: "", limit: 500 }) -> ok false, unknown argument "limit"
After: not built - the caller to fix is examples/journey (never touched by a sweep) and the schema change is a tool contract with that consumer
Method: probe - the two searches and the door run in node on the seed; the journey itself was not run (it boots dev servers)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a handler test in test/spatial-model-tools.test.ts walking search_records { text: "", page: n } until showing sums to of (276), plus the journey act 3 run by the director once its call pages
